# C++ & SWIG Development Guide (ezsnmp)

Use this skill when developing, refactoring, or fixing bugs in the C++ layer, SWIG interface files, or Python-C++ bindings for `ezsnmp`.

## 1. Architecture & Source File Boundaries

The C++ layer bridges Python to the underlying Net-SNMP C library using SWIG (Simplified Wrapper and Interface Generator) and modern C++17.

```
ezsnmp/
├── include/              # Public C++ header files (.h)
├── interface/            # SWIG interface definition files (.i)
└── src/
    ├── datatypes.cpp       # SNMP data type conversion (ASN.1 to Python)
    ├── exceptionsbase.cpp  # C++ exception class definitions
    ├── helpers.cpp         # Mutex locking, GIL management, error helpers
    ├── sessionbase.cpp     # Base SNMP session management logic
    ├── thread_safety.cpp   # Multi-threading and synchronization primitives
    └── net-snmp-5.10-final-patched/
        ├── snmpbulkget.cpp # SNMP GETBULK operation
        ├── snmpbulkwalk.cpp# SNMP BULKWALK operation
        ├── snmpget.cpp     # SNMP GET operation
        ├── snmpgetnext.cpp # SNMP GETNEXT operation
        ├── snmpset.cpp     # SNMP SET operation
        ├── snmptrap.cpp    # SNMP TRAP / INFORM operation
        └── snmpwalk.cpp    # SNMP WALK operation
```

> [!CRITICAL]
> **Never modify SWIG-generated files directly**:
> - Forbidden: `ezsnmp/src/ezsnmp_*.cpp` (`ezsnmp_datatypes.cpp`, `ezsnmp_sessionbase.cpp`, etc.)
> - Forbidden: Autogenerated root Python wrappers (`ezsnmp/datatypes.py`, `ezsnmp/sessionbase.py`, etc.)
> Always edit the `.i` interface file in `ezsnmp/interface/` or the source `.cpp` files, and recompile.

---

## 2. C++17 Standard & Coding Standards

1. **Standard**: All code must conform strictly to **C++17** (`-std=c++17`).
2. **Memory Safety & RAII**:
   - Wrap raw pointers and dynamically allocated structures in RAII guards or `std::unique_ptr` where possible.
   - Always free Net-SNMP PDUs via `snmp_free_pdu(pdu)` in all execution branches (including exceptions).
   - Clean up Net-SNMP session structs properly (`snmp_close(session)` or `netsnmp_cleanup_session(session)`).
3. **Clang-Format**:
   Code must be formatted according to `.clang-format`:
   ```bash
   clang-format -i ezsnmp/src/*.cpp ezsnmp/src/net-snmp-5.10-final-patched/*.cpp ezsnmp/include/*.h
   ```

---

## 3. Thread Safety & Python GIL Management

1. **Releasing the GIL**:
   Blocking network calls to Net-SNMP (`snmp_synch_response`, `snmp_sess_synch_response`) must release the Python GIL to allow concurrent threads to run:
   ```cpp
   Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS
   status = snmp_sess_synch_response(ss, pdu, &response);
   Py_END_ALLOW_THREADS
   ```
2. **Re-acquiring the GIL**:
   Never touch Python objects, raise Python exceptions, or call Python C API functions inside a `Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS` block.
3. **Session Locks**:
   Use mutex synchronization in `helpers.cpp` / `thread_safety.cpp` to prevent data races when multiple threads access the same session handle.

---

## 4. Local Build & In-Place Verification

To compile the C++ extension locally for testing:

```bash
# Build C++ extension in-place within the repository
/home/carlkidcrypto/Github/ezsnmp/python3.12.venv/bin/python setup.py build_ext --inplace

# Verify with Python test suite
/home/carlkidcrypto/Github/ezsnmp/python3.12.venv/bin/pytest python_tests/

# Verify with C++ unit tests
cd cpp_tests && ninja -C build test
```
